Salesforce, Kroger and Dollar General Report in the Earnings Week of November 30
sum: The short answer. It is a full trading week with no market holiday, and Canada’s five big banks are the heaviest group, all reporting Wednesday or Thursday. Salesforce reports Wednesday evening and Marvell holds its call Tuesday at 4:30 p.m. ET.

Kroger, which cut its store sales forecast in September, and Dollar General hold their calls Thursday morning, two reports on what shoppers spend on groceries and everyday goods. The November jobs report comes out Friday at 8:30 a.m. ET, a day with no big company on the calendar. Every company worth $10 billion or more has set its own date; for seven of them, Nasdaq’s calendar has not caught up yet.

Marvell on Tuesday and Salesforce on Wednesday lead the US technology names. Kroger, Dollar General and Royal Bank of Canada hold their calls Thursday morning, and four more Canadian banks report on Wednesday and Thursday.

Salesforce, the largest US company reporting this week, releases its results Wednesday after the market closes, with a call at 5:00 p.m. ET. In its August 26 release, it forecast $11.42 billion to $11.5 billion of revenue for this quarter, up 11% to 12% from a year earlier. It is also Salesforce’s first report since its October 20 deal to acquire Braze, a customer engagement software company, for cash.

Marvell, a chipmaker that sells heavily to data centers, holds its call Tuesday at 4:30 p.m. ET, after its results. Its August 27 release forecast about $3.15 billion of revenue for this quarter, give or take 5%, after a record $2.739 billion in the second quarter. Marvell said then that it was “again raising” its revenue outlook for its next two fiscal years. On November 2 it agreed to acquire Lumentum, a maker of optical parts, paying in Marvell shares.

Kroger, the supermarket chain, holds its call Thursday at 8:00 a.m. ET. In its September 11 release, it lowered its forecast for identical sales without fuel, its measure of sales at existing stores leaving out gas. It now expects growth of 0.2% to 0.8% for the year, down from 1.0% to 2.0%. It kept its forecast for adjusted earnings, a measure that leaves out some one-off items.
Dollar General holds its call Thursday at 9:00 a.m. ET, on the day of its results. Its August 27 release raised its forecast for the year to about $7.80 to $8.00 of earnings a share.

Royal Bank vs. a Canadian Bank ETF: Which Would I Choose for My First $10,000?
sum: Picking your first bank investment can feel like choosing the strongest umbrella before a Canadian spring. A familiar name is reassuring, but you still want to know what happens when the weather turns. With $10,000 to invest, the choice is also about how much risk exposure you want to one company.

Banks earn money from lending, payments, wealth management, and other financial services. Lower loan losses or stronger client activity can lift earnings. A weaker economy can reverse the picture, especially when borrowers struggle and banks set aside more money for potential defaults.

An individual bank gives you its particular strengths and weaknesses. A bank exchange-traded fund (ETF) spreads the investment across several lenders, reducing the impact of one company’s mistakes. It still leaves you exposed to the same sector and many of the same economic pressures.
Understanding how ETFs work also means checking fees and overlap. Owning a bank fund alongside several bank stocks may concentrate a portfolio more than its number of holdings suggests.

Royal Bank of Canada (TSX: RY) combines Canadian banking with substantial wealth-management and capital-markets operations. That mix lets it earn from household borrowing, client assets, and financial transactions, rather than relying on one source of revenue.

Its recent earnings show why shareholders value that breadth. Third-quarter adjusted earnings reached $4.28 per share, up 11% from a year earlier. Full-year 2025 adjusted earnings were $14.43 per share. Continued client activity and business growth support the investment case, although capital-markets revenue can fluctuate.

At writing, the $285.69 share price is about 19.8 times those 2025 adjusted earnings. That said, credit deterioration or slower earnings growth could make that premium uncomfortable. Royal reports its fourth-quarter and full-year results on December 3. Until then, the third-quarter numbers are the latest reported results, not a completed fiscal 2026 earnings record.

Royal Bank of Canada Stock (RY) Moved Up by 3.28% on Nov 23: What Signal Does It Send?
sum: Royal Bank of Canada (RY) moved up by 3.28%. The Banking & Investment Services sector is up by 3.02%. The company outperformed the industry. Top 3 stocks by turnover in the sector: Goldman Sachs Group Inc (GS) up 4.56%; JPMorgan Chase & Co (JPM) up 2.54%; Citigroup Inc (C) up 3.98%.

Royal Bank of Canada advanced firmly during trading, driven by renewed institutional optimism surrounding the North American banking sector, stabilizing interest rate expectations, and strong positioning ahead of fiscal year-end financial reporting. As central banks navigate their monetary policy adjustments, easing concerns over rapid credit deterioration have revitalized demand for high-quality commercial lenders. A more constructive economic outlook in Canada, coupled with resilient employment and consumer spending data, has alleviated systemic fears regarding residential mortgage renewals and retail credit distress, supporting broad-based buying across Canadian tier-one financials.

Fundamentally, the lender is benefiting from healthier net interest margin dynamics and improving operational leverage. With bond yields stabilizing and the yield curve demonstrating constructive steepening, the pressure on deposit costs has begun to moderate, offering tailwinds to lending margins. Concurrently, momentum across global investment banking and advisory activities has fueled revenue expectations for the bank’s capital markets division. Furthermore, strategic integration and cost-optimization efforts within its U.S. wealth management and commercial banking platforms, notably City National, are reinforcing investor confidence that previously troublesome efficiency drags are being systematically resolved.

From a market strategy perspective, the upward momentum is reinforced by institutional portfolio rotations favoring defensively positioned financial institutions with disciplined capital allocation and robust CET1 capital buffers. As the fiscal fourth-quarter earnings season approaches, sell-side sentiment has turned increasingly constructive, with several market participants lifting earnings forecasts on the back of lower anticipated provisions for credit losses and steady dividend coverage.

Royal Bank of Canada stock: RBC agrees to buy Yarra Capital Management
sum: Royal Bank of Canada agreed on November 9, 2026, to acquire full ownership of Yarra Capital Management, an Australian investment manager focused on fixed income, equities and alternative investment solutions. The announcement was carried by TMX Money from RBC's Canada NewsWire release.

Yarra, founded in 2017, has offices in Melbourne and Sydney and manages approximately A$18 billion as of September 30, 2026. The firm has approximately 75 employees and serves Australian institutional and retail investors.

RBC Global Asset Management said Yarra's investment and distribution capabilities complement its existing business. RBC said the transaction is intended to expand its capabilities and diversify its market share beyond North America, including in Australia and the wider Asia-Pacific region.

RBC said completion is expected in the first quarter of 2027 and remains subject to customary closing conditions, including regulatory approval. The bank also said the transaction is not expected to have a significant impact on its common equity Tier 1 ratio or future run-rate earnings.

Over the past 3 years the stock has gained 143.8%, which raises the stakes on whether Royal Bank of Canada’s return on capital can justify such a strong move.

The planned acquisition of Australian asset manager Yarra Capital Management, with about A$18b in assets under management, may support expectations for fee based income and capital efficient growth in the asset management arm if it integrates as planned.
The issue now is whether the returns Royal Bank of Canada earns on its capital are strong enough and durable enough to make today's share price look well supported on that basis.

Royal Bank Of Canada And 2 Other Top Canadian Dividend Stocks
sum: Rising U.S. inflation and talk of higher interest rates have put reliable income back in the spotlight for Canadian investors. Cash in a savings account feels safer, but it does not grow its payout in the same way a business can increase its dividend. Royal Bank of Canada stock gains appeal from cash-back overhaul
sum: Royal Bank of Canada announced enhanced rewards for two cash-back credit cards on Monday, November 2, 2026. The changes affect the RBC Cash Back Mastercard and the RBC Cash Back Preferred World Elite Mastercard, with new earning structures already in effect and more flexible redemptions planned for December.

FT.com reported that RBC added uncapped cash-back earning rates across everyday spending categories. The standard RBC Cash Back Mastercard now offers 2% on groceries, 1% on gas, electric-vehicle charging, rideshare and transit, and 0.5% on other net purchases.

The Preferred World Elite card offers 3% on groceries, dining, gas, electric-vehicle charging, transit, rideshare, streaming and digital gaming. Other net purchases earn 1%. The card also adds out-of-province and out-of-country emergency medical coverage, flight-delay and delayed-baggage insurance, and mobile-device insurance.

RBC said the new earning structures took effect automatically for existing and new cardholders on October 1, 2026. The standard card retains its zero-dollar annual fee. The Preferred World Elite card carries a $120 annual fee for the primary cardholder and $50 for each additional cardholder.

Starting December 2, cardholders will be able to redeem cash back at any time through RBC Online Banking or the RBC Mobile app once their balance reaches $1. RBC said balances can be checked through either channel and rewards will accumulate indefinitely. The announcement also gives cardholders more control over when they claim rewards instead of relying on a scheduled payout.

For investors, the announcement expands RBC's consumer-card proposition rather than changing the bank's earnings outlook. The immediate focus is execution: the new rates must support customer engagement while the lower redemption threshold and digital access simplify the reward process.

TD vs. Royal Bank: Which Dividend Stock Would I Buy With $10,000?
sum: Choosing a bank for your next $10,000 can feel like choosing between two familiar branches on the same street. The businesses differ once you follow the earnings. One offers a recovery opportunity with more repair work. The other offers a broader earnings mix at a price that already reflects much of its strength. I’d let that tradeoff decide the purchase before a small yield difference gets too much attention.

Toronto-Dominion Bank (TSX: TD) combines a major Canadian retail franchise with substantial U.S. operations and wholesale banking. Its domestic customer base gives it a strong foundation. The U.S. business adds opportunity, alongside the compliance work and operating constraints that have shaped its recent strategy. I’d view the stock as an established bank working through a specific recovery, with a demanding route back to stronger growth.

Third-quarter adjusted earnings reached $2.77 per share, up 26% year over year. That’s encouraging evidence that the recovery is reaching each share. Its common equity tier 1 ratio was 14.3%, providing a substantial capital buffer. Together, the figures support the case that TD can continue rewarding shareholders while funding the work needed to improve the business.

The $1.12 quarterly dividend, or $4.48 annualized, uses about 40% of the latest adjusted quarterly earnings. The catch is execution in the United States. Regulatory constraints and compliance costs can keep the bank from using all its strengths as freely as investors would like, which is the price of owning the recovery opportunity.

Royal Bank of Canada (TSX: RY) adds substantial wealth management, commercial banking, insurance, and capital-markets operations to its retail banking base. That gives it more ways to earn than Canadian mortgage and deposit growth alone. I’d favour that mix for an investor wanting a bank they can hold through changing conditions without depending on one turnaround programme delivering exactly on schedule.

Its third-quarter adjusted earnings were $4.28 per share, up 11%, with a common equity tier 1 ratio of 13.5%. The quarterly dividend is $1.76, consuming about 41% of that adjusted earnings figure. Both banks therefore have meaningful room behind their latest payments, even though the growth rates and capital ratios differ.

RBC Launches Auto-Callable Enhanced Return Barrier Notes Linked to Five Major U.S. Bank Stocks, Maturing 2029
sum: On November 4, 2026, Royal Bank of Canada filed a free writing prospectus outlining the terms for Auto-Callable Enhanced Return Barrier Notes tied to a basket of five prominent U.S. financial-sector equities, with maturity set for November 29, 2029.
- Issuer and CUSIP: The Notes are issued by Royal Bank of Canada (CUSIP 78018DRB5), traded on NYSE under the ticker RY.

- Basket Composition: The basket includes five equally weighted stocks: Bank of America (BAC), Citigroup (C), Goldman Sachs (GS), Morgan Stanley (MS), and Wells Fargo (WFC), each representing 20% of the basket.

- Auto-Call Feature: If on November 30, 2027, the basket’s closing value is at or above the Initial Basket Value of 100, the Notes will be automatically called, with investors receiving a minimum of $1,132.50 per $1,000 principal, equating to at least 113.25% of principal.

- Enhanced Return at Maturity: Should the Notes not be called and the Final Basket Value exceed the Initial Basket Value, investors will earn a return equal to 150% of the Basket Return, as detailed in the filing.

- Barrier Level: The Barrier Value is set at 70, which is 70% of the Initial Basket Value; if the Final Basket Value falls below this threshold, investors will incur a loss of 1% of principal for every 1% decline below the Initial Basket Value.
- Initial Estimated Value: The filing estimates the initial value to range between $902.50 and $952.50 per $1,000 principal, which is below the public offering price.

Capitalize on the shift in consumer banking that Royal Bank of Canada is leaning into by scanning a curated shortlist of other issuers with rich rewards programs in the 5 high quality undervalued stocks.
Bulls see Royal Bank of Canada using richer rewards to lock in everyday spending, while bears focus on richer benefits compressing card economics. Which argument fits the current valuation best?

Royal Bank of Canada last closed at CA$286.21 against a widely followed fair value estimate of CA$302.43. This frames the richer rewards push as part of a broader story about fee income, AI and capital deployment.

The main thing that has to go right is that Royal Bank of Canada continues to convert its AI rollout, Global Transaction Banking build out, and HSBC Canada and City National integrations into sustained fee income growth and durable cost efficiencies despite ongoing credit and macro pressures.

The current valuation implies that the market is not fully crediting Royal Bank of Canada for its recent 17.9 to 18% ROE on a 13.5% CET1 ratio, its realized HSBC Canada synergies, and the targeted $700 million to $1 billion AI contribution by 2027.

sum: On October 28, 2026, the Bank of Canada raised its policy rate by 0.25%, marking the first hike since July 2023. The central bank held the benchmark steady at 2.25% for seven consecutive meetings before sounding the alarm. Inflation spiked to 3.1% in September 2026, sending policymakers on high alert.

During the post-meeting press conference on Wednesday, Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem explained the monetary policy decision. He cited the Middle East oil shock and unresolved Canada-US trade relations as major reasons for the upward rate adjustment to 2.5%. Macklem is increasingly worried about inflation risks.

In response, TSX declined modestly by 0.04% the day after and remains up 14.3% year-to-date. However, if more rate hikes are on the horizon, investor sentiment could shift. They could rotate from rate-sensitive sectors and speculative growth stocks into lower-risk investments. Energy, for one, continues to benefit directly from surging oil prices. Banks could see higher margins on loans and mortgages.

Royal Bank of Canada (TSX: RY) will hold up regardless of the economic environment. The $396.5 billion bank is the largest TSX company by market capitalization. Its scale and diversified business model provide peace of mind, not to mention the 156-year dividend track record.

President and CEO David McKay said Royal Bank of Canada continues to raise the bar globally to deliver exceptional, record results. In Q3 fiscal 2026, net income rose 11% to a record $6 billion versus Q3 fiscal 2025. For the nine months ended July 31, 2026, provision for credit losses (PCL) fell 10.5% year-over-year to $3 billion.

RY trades at $288.21 per share (+26.4% year-to-date) and pays a 2.5% dividend. Look beyond the price, as you’d be investing in a bedrock of stability and an anchor stock. The banking giant increased its prime rate by 25 basis points to 4.7% effective October 29, 2026. It will expand its net interest margin capacity

Canadian Natural Resources (TSX: CNQ) is a solid choice for long-term dividend income and capital growth. Notably, Macklem said rising inflation is energy-driven. This large-cap energy major boasts long-life, low-decline oil sands assets, allowing for consistent production increases. It also operates on exceptionally low break-even costs.
